title: Comparing the hydrolysis of alkyl bromides
body: A student studied the hydrolysis of two alkyl bromides with hydroxide ion. For compound P, tert-butyl bromide (CH3)3CBr, in a polar protic solvent, doubling the concentration of the bromide doubled the initial rate, but doubling the concentration of hydroxide ion did not change the rate at all. For compound Q, bromomethane CH3Br, doubling either the concentration of the bromide or the concentration of hydroxide ion doubled the initial rate. The student then compared two benzylic bromides under conditions that favour ionisation of the C-Br bond: benzyl bromide, C6H5CH2Br, and compound R, C6H5CH(C6H5)Br, in which the carbon bearing bromine carries two phenyl groups.
